answer: Scarce resource: verified physical custody time. Each identity must periodically solve a cipher challenge embedded in a hardware token bound to a unique onyx substrate, whose micro-structure is logged at issue and checked at each renewal. An agent can forge software identities freely, but each renewal requires the token to have spent real hours in continuous physical possession. Attacker cost: acquiring and holding distinct substrates and idle custody time per identity, which scales linearly and cannot be parallelized without genuine hardware.
